title: Nabhani Dynasty
capsule: The Nabhani (Bani Nabhan) dynasty were an Arab ruling house of Azdi tribal origin that dominated the Omani interior from the mid-twelfth century until 1624. They came to power around 1154 after the expulsion of Seljuk influence and ruled as muluk (kings), reducing the elected Imamate to a ceremonial function while controlling the frankincense trade routes that connected Oman's interior to Baghdad and Damascus. Their capital at Bahla became the site of a massive fortification complex — today a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Portuguese seizure of Muscat in 1507 and progressive coastal dominance pressured the dynasty, which held the interior until Nasir bin Murshid of the Yaruba dynasty took control in 1624.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Nabhani period is known primarily from later Omani chronicle tradition (the Kashf al-Ghumma) and Portuguese sources; the precise extent of their control beyond the Bahla-centred interior is poorly documented.
